item.title: Cave-inspired 3D printed Japanese home touted as earthquake resistant — two-story house first of its kind to be granted seismic compliance certificate
item.description: Construction of the first government approved two-story 3D printed home has been completed in Japan. The design is 'cave-inspired.'

item.description: Starlink’s official social media channels are boasting about an incredible performance update on the way to mobile customers.

item.title: Entry-level PC market to ‘disappear’ by 2028 — rising memory prices pile more strain on consumer PC market
item.description: A 130% surge in combined DRAM and SSD prices by the end of 2026 will push PC prices up 17% compared to 2025 levels and wipe out the sub-$500 PC market.

item.description: Rebellions details how it developed one of the world's first quad-chiplet AI accelerator with UCIe interconnects and how it did not use all of the technologies that the UCIe 1.0 specifications includes.

item.title: Exploring the future of Artificial Intelligence — today's models, tomorrow's agents, and the big privacy problem
item.description: The world of AI is getting more complex, and we assess the current state of LLMs, what makes them tick, and explore the risks and features that companies are looking to integrate in the future.

item.title: Transcend 260S 2TB SSD Review: A Dependable Alternative PCIe 5.0 Contender
item.description: The Transcend 260S is not a record-setter but it does deliver consistent performance in what should be a reliable package.

item.title: Nvidia releases new GeForce 595.71 driver to fix serious fan control bug — new update resolves issues for RTX 30, 40, and 50-series GPUs that reportedly stopped some fans from working
item.description: A new Nvidia GPU driver, 595.71, has been released which resolves issues in its since-recalled 595.59 driver which reportedly caused some graphics card fans to stop working.
